target: Round 19 route "extension-complexity": the level-j choice lift R_j(G), the invariant lev(G), the exit bound, the router-tree level-two theorem, and the value polytope V(G)
verdict:
I rebuilt every game and every number from the route's STATEMENTS (not its code) in exact rational arithmetic, with my own SSG core (trap test, brute-force w* over all positional pairs, exact first-passage rows) and my own two-phase exact simplex, cross-validated against brute-force vertex enumeration on 300 random LPs and against the paper's own independent datum (max_{R_1} x(v_1) = 3/5 on W_14 of rem:choice-lift, reproduced exactly by my lift). Work in /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/c506180a-e393-4ffa-a18f-efc78c98397e/scratchpad/r19-audit-extension-complexity-correctness/.

WHAT REPRODUCES. The headline holds. On prop:router-tree's OWN 10-vertex T_1(2,3/8) (the route built a 12-vertex variant; see finding 6) I get stopping, w* = 3/8 at all three Max vertices, sum-over-C ranges [9/8,3], [9/8,3/2], [9/8,9/8] at j = 0,1,2, root level-one interval [3/8,6/11] exactly as prop:router-tree records, so lev(T_1) = 2. On the paper's 14-vertex T_2(2,3/8) I get max_{R_1} sum = 72/17 exactly from the FULL lift (no symmetry reduction), root faces 39/11, depth-one faces 219/56, leaf feedback faces R_1 ∩ F^0_l INFEASIBLE (confirmed by a primal feasibility LP, not only by dual unboundedness), leaf constant faces 21/8; with the valid half of xc:balas-iter and x >= w* this gives R_2 = {w*}, so lev(T_2) = 2 independently of symlift.py. T_3: max_{R_1} sum = 10.1379310344828 = 294/29 and max_{R_2} sum = 5.625 = 45/8 in floating point. CYC(3,2,3/8) rebuilt from its statement: 20 vertices, stopping, w* = 3/8, merged matrix 3/4(J - I) with Perron root 3/2, (I-M)^{-1} carrying -2/7 and -6/7, and R_1 = {w*}; all three Max vertices splitters. The exit matrix on T_1 is exactly K = [[0,0,1],[0,0,3/4],[0,3/4,0]] with (I-K)^{-1} >= 0, and at j = 1 K = M with rho(M) = sqrt(3/2) > 1; on CYC at j = 2 K is transient. AND reproduces exactly (w* = (1/4,1/8,1/4,1/2,1/8), the four occupancies (1,0,1,0),(3/2,0,0,1),(0,1,1,0),(0,3/2,0,1), and lambda = (3/2,-1,-3/2,1) with sum lambda f = 0 and sum lambda val = (-1/8,1/8)). The ladder identity phi_i(val_sigma) = XOR_{k>=i} sigma_k holds for all 2^n strategies at n = 2..12 with image size 2^n. lev = 1 holds on prop:own-stall's R and on rem:own-stall's seven-vertex game verified PER COORDINATE (stronger than the route's own test), and G8, S, S_r, H_m do have |C| = 1. I reconstructed the proofs of xc:conditioning, xc:level-one, xc:exit, xc:yannakakis (both directions), xc:reduction, xc:ladder, xc:occ and xc:onectrl; all are correct up to the small gaps below.

WHAT BREAKS. One clause of a lemma marked proved is FALSE, and I refuted it with an explicit 13-vertex stopping SSG (BALASITER_COUNTEREXAMPLE.json), all of whose non-sinks are reachable from its start: xc:balas-iter's closing "Consequently a necessary condition for lev(G) >= j+2 is that R_j(G) cap F_v^i is nonempty for every v and both i". Two further defects are reporting defects of the kind round 18 was told to stop making: an extrapolation from two exact data points asserted inside a proposition, and a large body of floating-point search reported under a heading that says "All exact unless stated". None of these touches the headline, so the route keeps new-theorem material, but sound = false.

findings.result_name: The hierarchy is a Balas iteration, and the emptiness test that closes it (lem xc:balas-iter)
findings.defect: The lemma's closing sentence -- "Consequently a necessary condition for lev(G) >= j+2 is that R_j(G) cap F_v^i is nonempty for every v in C and both i" -- does not follow from the proved part and is FALSE. The proved part gives only R_{j+1} subset R_j cap F_v^{1-i} when R_j cap F_v^i is empty; that inclusion does not make R_{j+1} equal {w*}, which is what lev <= j+1 requires. The same false criterion is carried into next_steps as the design rule for a level-three instance ("a level-three instance must keep BOTH faces alive at EVERY controlled vertex"), so the route's stated search plan rests on it.
findings.evidence: Counterexample built and verified exactly, /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/c506180a-e393-4ffa-a18f-efc78c98397e/scratchpad/r19-audit-extension-complexity-correctness/t_balasiter.py and BALASITER_COUNTEREXAMPLE.json. G' has 13 vertices, t0 = 11, t1 = 12, kinds ['max','max','max','avg','avg','avg','avg','avg','max','avg','avg'] and succ [(1,2),(3,5),(3,5),(0,4),(0,11),(11,6),(12,7),(12,11),(11,9),(12,11),(0,8)]: it is prop:router-tree's T_1(2,3/8) (vertices 0,1,2 Max; 3,4 the c-chain; 5,6,7 the 3/8-chain) plus a Max vertex p = 8 whose action 0 is t0 and whose action 1 is the average vertex 9 -> (t1,t0) of value 1/2, plus a start average vertex 10 -> (root, p). Machine-checked: stopping by the trap test of lem:trapchar; every non-sink reachable from the start 10; C = {0,1,2,8}; w*|_C = (3/8,3/8,3/8,1/2). At j = 0 the face R_0 cap F_p^0 (the LP with the extra pin x(p) = 0) is INFEASIBLE, while R_0 cap F_p^1 is feasible. Yet the per-coordinate ranges over R_1 are x(root) in [3/8,6/11], x(l_1) = x(l_2) in [3/8,21/44], x(p) = 1/2, so R_1 is not {w*}; the ranges over R_2 are all single points equal to w*, so lev(G') = 2. Thus a face is empty at level j = 0 and lev = 2 = j+2, contradicting the claimed necessary condition. (The other half of the lemma, R_{j+1} subset B(R_j) and its use in xc:why-two to close T_2 at level two, is correct and is what my independent proof of lev(T_2) = 2 uses.)

findings.result_name: The router tree stops the choice hierarchy at level two (prop xc:stops(b) / JSON result 4)
findings.defect: An unproved extrapolation from three data points is stated as part of a proposition marked proved: "so the asymptotic vacuity of prop:router-tree is a level-one phenomenon and does not grow with d" (tex), and in the JSON "the asymptotic vacuity of level one proved in prop:router-tree does not lift to level two". lev is computed exactly only at d = 1 and d = 2; d = 3 is floating point. Nothing in the route proves lev(T_d) = 2 for d >= 3 or bounds lev(T_d) at all as d grows, and prop:router-tree's vacuity statement is precisely an asymptotic one, so the negation of it for level two is exactly the claim not established.
findings.evidence: results.tex xc:stops(b) and xc:measured; the exact runs cover d = 1, 2 only ("T_3(2,3/8) ... the target 45/8 at j=2 in FLOATING POINT only, the exact run was cut short"). I reproduced d = 1 and d = 2 exactly (lev = 2 in both) and d = 3 in floating point only (max_{R_2} sum = 5.6250000000000036 against 45/8), so I can confirm the two exact rows and cannot confirm the family claim either. Under the round-18 lesson ("your headline is a claim: it must be a sentence you PROVED") the clause must be deleted or restated as measured at d <= 3.

findings.result_name: The measurement report behind xc:frontier and xc:measured (the 848 197 abstract systems, the 84 691 random games) and the two-player level criterion
findings.defect: Two independent reporting defects. (a) EXACTNESS: xc:measured opens "All exact unless stated" and then reports "261 751 systems with |C| in {4,5} ... level computed to exactness", "389 406 further systems ... of which 5 732 failed at level one and every one of those was exact at level two", "27 203 systems with general dyadic rows", "169 716 flat systems" and "84 691 random stopping games with |C| in {3,4}" without marking them floating point. Every one of those runs goes through flift.maxR, which is scipy/HiGHS in double precision with acceptance tolerances 1e-8 and 1e-7; flift.py's own docstring says "EXPLORATION ONLY", and fsearch.py's says "compute lev(G) approximately". No exact recertification was performed on any of them (there was nothing flagged to recertify). (b) CRITERION: the level test used everywhere in the search and in verify_stalls.py is max = min of the SINGLE functional sum_C x against sum_C w*. The route itself states in xc:measured that "with x >= w* (one player) the maximum of the sum suffices" -- i.e. the test is justified only with Vmin empty -- yet it is applied to systems with 1, 2 and 3 Min vertices and to the two-player instances. For a two-player game max = min of one functional only says R_j lies in a hyperplane through w*, not that R_j = {w*}, so the reported counts ("maximum level 2", "5 732 failed at level one") are not counts of the quantity defined by lev. The gap statement in the JSON repeats the 848 197 figure with no float or criterion caveat.
findings.evidence: /tmp/.../r19-extension-complexity/flift.py lines 1-2 and 17ff (numpy/linprog, method HiGHS); absearch.py:levf (tol=1e-8, calls maxR); run_abs.py, run_abs2.py, run_abs3.py, run_abs4.py all import maxR from flift; fsearch.py docstring and levf(tol=1e-7). verify_stalls.py:levex and verify_main.py:levex both accept when hi == tgt and lo == tgt for cvec = all-ones. I re-ran the two two-player instances PER COORDINATE with my own exact lift: on prop:own-stall's R (|C| = 5) R_1 pins every coordinate to w* (ranges (1/2,1/2),(1/2,1/2),(1/2,1/2),(0,0),(1/2,1/2)) and on rem:own-stall's seven-vertex game (|C| = 3) likewise (2/3,2/3,2/3), so those two published claims survive; the search counts do not have that backing. (t_twoplayer.py / t_twoplayer.log.)

findings.result_name: The level-j choice lift and the conditioning lemma (lem xc:conditioning)
findings.defect: The conditioning step is asserted where it needs a case. The proof says the family {w_{A u A',B u B'}, z_{A u A',B u B'}}_{|A'|+|B'| <= j-k}, divided by w_{A,B}, satisfies (L1)-(L4) at level j-k. It does not, as written: (L2) at the new level demands, for every v not in A' u B', the splitting w_{A',B'} = w_{A'+v,B'} + w_{A',B'+v}, and for v in A (already pinned) the index (A', B'+v) maps to (A u A', B u B' u {v}) whose two parts are NOT disjoint, so the required variable does not exist in the old certificate. The repair is one line -- declare every pair whose A' meets B or whose B' meets A to be (w,z) = (0,0), which satisfies (L2), (L3) and (L4) vacuously and telescopes correctly -- but it is absent, and the conditioning lemma is what R_j subset D_j, xc:exit and xc:balas-iter all rest on.
findings.evidence: results.tex, proof of xc:conditioning, sentence beginning "Conditioning: rescaling (L3) by w_{A,B} > 0 gives ...". The gap is only in the write-up; with the repair every downstream use is sound, and all my numerical checks of R_j subset D_j behaviour are consistent.

findings.defect: The proof writes the row u >= p^{v,i} u + q^{v,i} as u >= q^{v,i}/(1-p^{v,i}) = val_i(v) without noting that p^{v,i} < 1. If p^{v,i} = 1 (necessarily q^{v,i} = 0) the row is the tautology 0 >= 0 and F_v^i is all of Qt, not a point, and the argument collapses. The missing sentence: on a stopping game the action i at the unique controlled vertex v cannot return to v with probability one, since the positional strategy playing i would then never reach a sink.
findings.evidence: results.tex, proof of xc:onectrl. The lemma is true; the hypothesis is available and unstated. It carries xc:stops(a) for G8, S, S_r(2), S_r(3), H_2, H_3, H_4, all of which I confirmed have |C| = 1 from myinst.py.

findings.result_name: games_built: T_1, T_2, T_3 of prop:router-tree
findings.defect: The games recorded as "T_1(2,3/8) of prop:router-tree", "T_2(2,3/8)", "T_3(2,3/8)" are not the instances the cited proposition defines. prop:router-tree fixes N = 2^{d+1}+e+D+1 with the damping chain c_1,...,c_e SHARED by all leaves, and states explicitly "T_1(2,3/8) on 10 vertices (3 Max, 5 average)"; the route gives every leaf its own chain, obtaining 12 vertices (3 Max, 7 average) at d = 1, 20 (7 Max, 11 average) at d = 2 and 36 at d = 3, against the paper's 10, 14 and 22. Since the level-j lift depends only on the first-passage data (p^{v,i}, q^{v,i}) over C, which is identical, no conclusion changes -- but the games_built field is required precisely so that the instance can be identified, and a reader comparing counts will not match them.
findings.evidence: prop:router-tree at frontier.tex l.16593ff; ROUTER1_GAME.json has 10 non-sinks with two separate c-chains (6 -> (0,7), 7 -> (0,10) and 8 -> (0,9), 9 -> (0,10)). I rebuilt the paper's own 10-vertex and 14-vertex instances (router.py in my directory) and every number the route reports came out identical: [9/8,3], [9/8,3/2], [9/8,9/8]; root [3/8,6/11]; 72/17; 39/11; 219/56; 21/8.

findings.defect: Two imprecisions in the remark that positions the theorem. (i) "Cref{xc:exit} is therefore the level-j form of that remark" overstates: at j = 1 the criterion is strictly WEAKER than rem:merged-matrix, not equal to it. The remark itself notes K dominates M entrywise, and transience of the larger matrix K is a stronger hypothesis than transience of M; rem:merged-matrix's own derivation avoids the self-loop renormalisation entirely, so xc:exit does not recover it at j = 1. (ii) "while M has the cycle weight 2g > 1" is not a cycle weight: on T_1 the two 2-cycles root-leaf-root each have weight g, and 2g = 3/2 is rho(M)^2, the trace of the second power. The conclusion (M not transient) is right.
findings.evidence: t_exit.py / t_exit2.py: on T_1 at j = 1, K = M = [[0,1,1],[3/4,0,0],[3/4,0,0]] with spectral radius 1.2247448713915892 = sqrt(3/2); at j = 2 with the route's sets, K = [[0,0,1],[0,0,3/4],[0,3/4,0]] and (I-K)^{-1} = [[1,12/7,16/7],[0,16/7,12/7],[0,12/7,16/7]] >= 0. On CYC(3,2,3/8) at j = 2 both natural choices of the sets S_v give a transient K (rho = 3/4), confirming the route's side claim.

findings.result_name: The factorisation theorem, and the only form in which extension complexity counts against prob:main (prop xc:reduction)
findings.defect: The proved content is the (<=) reduction: a polynomial-size extended formulation of V(G), computable in polynomial time, would put prob:main in P. The clause appended to it -- "an exponential lower bound on xc(V(G_n)) for an explicit family is thus the only form in which the extension complexity of a polytope bears on prob:main; a lower bound for a polytope one does not optimise over is not a barrier" -- is asserted, not proved, and is in fact misleading in the direction it points: an exponential lower bound on xc(V(G_n)) would rule out only the route of writing a small extended formulation of V(G), it would not be a barrier for prob:main at all, since w*(v_0) can be computed without ever representing V(G). A statement of the form "only X bears on Y" is a claim about all possible arguments and has no proof here.
findings.evidence: results.tex, prop xc:reduction, second and third sentences; JSON result 7 statement, final sentence. Both halves of xc:yannakakis check out as written (I reconstructed the LP-duality argument; the only slip is that the (>=) direction drops the equalities that the definition of xc explicitly allows in Q, and the argument still goes through because the equality multipliers vanish at every y^j in Q).

findings.result_name: The occupancy polytope does not carry the value vector (rem xc:coupled, second half of JSON result 8)
findings.defect: The negative half is exactly right and reproduces. The positive half is over-stated and partly unproved: (i) "V(G) is the affine image of the coupled occupancy polytope Y(G) := conv{(f^v_sigma)_{v in C}}" is stated without a one-player hypothesis, but V(G) is defined by val_sigma = the value against an OPTIMAL Min response, which is not the value of any single profile, so the identity fails as soon as Vmin is nonempty; (ii) "The coupling is exactly the complementarity f^v(u,0) f^{v'}(u,1) = 0" asserts that this complementarity CUTS OUT Y(G), which is nowhere proved -- Y(G) is defined as a convex hull, and no argument is given that the hull is the set of tuples satisfying the flow equations plus that complementarity.
findings.evidence: results.tex rem:coupled; JSON result 8 statement, final sentence. The four-point certificate itself I reproduced exactly from the game (t_and.py): w* = (1/4,1/8,1/4,1/2,1/8), f = (1,0,1,0),(3/2,0,0,1),(0,1,1,0),(0,3/2,0,1), val|_C = (0,0),(0,0),(1/4,0),(1/4,1/8), sum lambda = 0, sum lambda f = (0,0,0,0), sum lambda val = (-1/8,1/8).

findings.result_name: The router tree stops the choice hierarchy at level two -- the symmetry reduction
findings.defect: The exact number 294/29 for max_{R_1} sum on T_3, and the T_2 level-two run, come from symlift.py, whose justification is the one sentence "averaging over the tree automorphisms is legitimate because the instance and the objective sum_C x are invariant". That is not the whole argument: a child-swap automorphism of T_d exchanges the two SUCCESSORS of the swapped node, hence exchanges its two ACTIONS, so the induced action on the lift variables must exchange the A- and B-roles of that coordinate in (w_{A,B}, z_{A,B}); an implementation that merely relabels C would be averaging over a group that does not act on the feasible set. The conclusion is not in doubt here -- I obtained 72/17 on T_2 at j = 1 from the FULL lift with no symmetry, and lev(T_2) = 2 from the Balas-iteration argument with no symmetry, and 294/29 to 15 digits in floating point -- but the exact T_3 figure rests on the unexplained reduction.
findings.evidence: xc:measured; t_router2b.log (full exact lift on the paper's 14-vertex T_2: 72/17), t_faces.log (leaf feedback faces infeasible, leaf constant faces 21/8, root 39/11, depth-one 219/56), t_float.log (T_3 j=1 = 10.137931034482756 against 294/29 = 10.137931034482758).

findings.result_name: Level one is Balas' closure (prop xc:level-one)
findings.defect: For the novelty lens rather than correctness: the STATEMENT is already in the paper. rem:choice-lift says, of the round-17 route's lift, "the level-one set is Balas' disjunctive closure bigcap_{v in C} conv(F_v^0 u F_v^1) of the faces F_v^i". What is new is the proof, and that it is a proof for the route's own explicitly written level-j programme rather than for an unspecified one. The route's why_not_implied ("no proof that such a lift's level one coincides with Balas' closure") is accurate but should say that the identification itself is asserted in the paper.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex l.16563-16566. My implementation of the route's (L1)-(L4) reproduces the paper's own independent level-one datum exactly -- max_{R_1} x(v_1) = 3/5 on W_14, against max_{R_0} x(v_1) = 1 and w*(v_1) = 1/2 (t_w14.log) -- which is the strongest available check that the written definition and the computations agree.
